_doc: CA3 — fidelity ledger of volume-dependent SEGMENTATION capabilities, each explicitly marked UNTESTABLE-at-current-book with its named unlock. Source: DIRECTOR_RULING_COHORT_ASSIGNMENT_ACTIVATED_2026-07-27 §2 (world-side variety activated, company-side segmentation stays untestable) + DIRECTOR_RULING_POOL_VS_BOOK_LAMBDA_STANDS_2026-07-27 (an untestable organ must be RECORDED untestable, not scored as working). Activation of pool variety (CA1) is NOT testability of the book — this ledger holds that line. Gate + R15 both-ways: background/segmentation_testability_ledger.py.
min_book_note: min_book_for_testability is the NECESSARY floor: the ~12-cell price_sensitivity×tenure value knee (simulation/population_coverage.py) at the director's >=3-households-per-protected-cell tail floor => 12 * 3 = 36. Necessary, not sufficient (uneven marginals need more). A capability marked testable at a book below its floor is a claim-status defect; the gate reds on it. The book cannot cross this floor until acquisition is a decision variable, so the mechanical floor and the human unlock below coincide.
current_book_size_source: saas.customers.CUSTOMERS (static book). The gate is called WITH the book size, never reads it, so it stays a pure function (independence, R15 pattern-1).

capabilities.name: ~12-cell value-knee coverage of the actual BOOK
capabilities.description: The company's real customer book populates the price_sensitivity x tenure ~12-cell value knee densely enough that per-cell statistics are meaningful. Distinct from the POOL coverage report (CA2), which draws N=200 world-side — this is the book the company actually serves.
capabilities.reason: 18-customer book cannot populate 12 cells at the >=3-per-cell floor; most cells are empty or singletons, so any per-cell segmentation statistic is noise.
capabilities.unlock: acquisition becomes a decision variable — director growth/leverage session, registered as that session's FIRST item (DIRECTOR_RULING_POOL_VS_BOOK_LAMBDA_STANDS_2026-07-27). Do NOT build the acquisition organ ahead of that session.

capabilities.name: Per-segment customer lifetime value
capabilities.description: Stable CLV / cohort-economics estimates per segment cell (mean margin, retention-weighted value) that could drive segment-level investment or pricing.
capabilities.reason: A per-segment CLV mean over 0-2 customers/cell has no sampling stability; the estimate is dominated by individual idiosyncrasy, not segment structure.
capabilities.unlock: acquisition becomes a decision variable — director growth/leverage session (first item).

capabilities.name: Per-segment churn / retention rate
capabilities.description: Segment-level churn or retention rates measured against SIM ground truth (belief-vs-truth gap per segment).
capabilities.reason: Churn is a rare per-customer event; per-segment rates over singleton cells cannot distinguish signal from a single departure. The gap metric would score noise.
capabilities.unlock: acquisition becomes a decision variable — director growth/leverage session (first item).

capabilities.name: Per-segment activity-based cost-to-serve
capabilities.description: Cost-to-serve differentiation by segment (activity-based pricing lens: flat margin makes some customers net-negative — CLAUDE.md). Requires enough per-cell customers to separate segment effect from individual cost variance.
capabilities.reason: 18 customers cannot separate a segment-level cost-to-serve effect from per-customer variance; the differentiation would be fitted to individuals, not segments.
capabilities.unlock: acquisition becomes a decision variable — director growth/leverage session (first item).

capabilities.name: Segment-differentiated pricing validated against outcomes
capabilities.description: Pricing decisions differentiated by segment and validated against realised segment outcomes (switching, margin, satisfaction).
capabilities.reason: Outcome validation per segment needs a populated book; at 18 customers a segment-differentiated price cannot be A/B-evaluated against a segment cohort that does not exist.
capabilities.unlock: acquisition becomes a decision variable — director growth/leverage session (first item).
